sentences.text:
Author: B. Vijaysen Reddy
Bench: B. Vijaysen Reddy
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice B. Vijaysen Reddy
 Writ Petition No.6835 of 2023
Order:

The writ petition is filed to declare the notice bearing No.129/PD/CELL dated 24.01.2023 pertaining to Cr.No.2 of 2021 of the RGIA Police Station, Shamshabad, registered for the offences under Sections 419, 420, 468, 471 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860, as illegal,
arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 21 of the Constitution of India.

2. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that notice dated 24.01.2023, which is partially visible, as major part of it was torn, was pasted on the wall of the rented house of the petitioner purporting to summon the petitioner to face proceedings under the Telangana Prevention of Dangerous Activities of Bootleggers, Dacoits, Drug Offenders, Goondas, Immoral Traffic Offenders,
Land Grabbers, Spurious Seed Offenders, Insecticide Offenders, Fertilizer Offenders, Food Adulteration Offenders, Fake Document Offenders, Scheduled Commodities Offenders, Forest Offenders, Gaming Offenders, Sexual Offenders, Explosive Substances Offenders, Arms Offenders,
Cyber Crime Offenders and White Collar or Financial Offenders Act, 1986 (for short 'the Act').
The petitioner was falsely implicated in Cr.No.2 of 2021 alleging that he has created false documents and committed forgery to procure insurance for two wheelers.
The petitioner was enlarged on bail in the month of February 2021.
The respondents have arbitrarily invoked the provisions of the Act and harassing the petitioner for illegal gain.
3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader representing the learned Advocate General submitted that the writ petition is not maintainable.
The petitioner has to approach the concerned police to receive the preventive detention order.

When the police tried to serve the notice on the petitioner, the petitioner evaded service of notice and as such, proclamation notice was affixed on the house of the petitioner to show cause as to why he should not be declared as proclamation offender and further action should not be taken against him.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the wife of the petitioner is present in the Court and if copy of the preventive detention order is served, she would receive the same.

5. However, the same is objected to by the learned Assistant Government Pleader stating that as per the procedure prescribed, only the detenu should receive the order and if preventive detention is served on any other person, the petition would take undue advantage of non-service of the preventive detention order as required under law.

sentences.text: In view of the above, the writ petition is disposed of giving liberty to the petitioner to approach the Station House Officer, RGIA Police Station, for receiving the preventive order within a period of two (2) weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
The impugned notice dated 24.01.2023 is suspended for period of two (2) weeks.

It is made clear that if the petitioner does not receive the preventive detention order within the aforesaid period of two (2) weeks, the respondent police are at liberty to proceed with further action against the petitioner in accordance with law.
The miscellaneous petitions pending, if any, shall stand closed.
There shall be no order as to costs.

B. VIJAYSEN REDDY, J March 27, 2023 Note: Issue CC by 28.03.2023 (B/o) DSK E. Sairam Gupta vs The State Of Telangana on 27 March, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/71493227/
